tasks.short: Notify responsible parties of confirmed breaches, required remedies and possible consequences.

steps.what: Retrieve approved findings, recipient details and applicable obligations.
Determine appropriate warning, remedy, deadline and escalation within delegated authority.
Prepare warning using findings, approved wording and notice instructions.
Approve wording, proportionality, recipient and authority to issue the warning.
Explain the approved warning, required remedies and available response channels.
Record delivery, response and remedy deadlines in the case record.

tasks.design: Configure the {WORKFLOW} to assemble approved findings and generate notices from controlled templates in the {DOCS}. Approval unlocks the specific notice and recipient; the compliance officer handles the conversation. A short structured response form creates the case record and schedules remedy reminders in the {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence, templates and delivery records were separated. Consequences often depended on judgement and delegated authority.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing approval and template features handle much of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting evidence and deadline records.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed facts, proportionality and sensitive conversations remain difficult. A company compliance officer usually cannot impose public-law penalties.
tasks.human_edge: Explain consequences fairly, recognise contested facts and distinguish a warning from a threat beyond company authority.

ambition.what: Twice-weekly triage of overdue high-risk remedies

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into assembling notices and chasing dates. The officer can propose remedy escalations twice weekly; sanction and enforcement rights do not expand.

reach.task: Prioritise overdue remedies by financial exposure.
reach.learn: Exposure estimation, risk appetite and escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: Controlled templates, approval routing and reminders can automate warning administration; these time shares are estimates.
GDPR Article 22 requires assessment when solely automated decisions significantly affect a natural person.

assumptions: The officer communicates company compliance findings within delegated authority.
Approved notice templates cover routine warnings; unusual wording stays with a person.
The approval in s4 supplies the action gate in s5.
The split retains substantial judgement and conversation time despite the automation prior.
Build ranges are estimates in working days and include national consultation where applicable; formal procedures may take longer.
unknowns: Who may approve warnings, contractual consequences and regulator referrals?
What proportion of warnings requires a live conversation?
Are recipient details, delivery evidence and deadlines available through supported interfaces?
Which national consultation requirements apply to case tracking?
research_questions: Which warnings can use fixed wording without weakening explanation or response rights?
What delivery evidence is required for each notice category?
new_work: Maintain notice templates and delegated-authority limits.
Review delivery failures and incorrect recipient details.
Confirm structured response records after sensitive conversations.
Handle disputed notices and overdue remedies.

tasks.short: Review applications and supporting records for eligibility, obligations and potential liability.

steps.what: Receive the application and register its supporting documents.
Check identifiers, dates and financial records against required fields.
Read supporting documents and extract facts relevant to eligibility or liability.

loop.input: Case documents and a fixed list of required facts.
loop.output: Typed facts with document references, exact supporting passages and unresolved gaps.
loop.check: Validate field types and source locations; a person verifies material facts and contradictions.
loop.stop: One extraction pass and one correction pass per document; unreadable or conflicting evidence goes to the officer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative documents express relevant facts in varied wording; field mappings handle only structured submissions.

steps.what: Assess eligibility or liability and identify unresolved questions.
Request missing evidence from the applicant or responsible party.
Finalise findings or record that the assessment awaits further evidence.

tasks.design: A case register in the {WORKFLOW} links submissions in the {DOCS} to deterministic checks on the {ERP}. A bounded extraction loop creates a source-linked evidence pack; the officer assesses contested facts and approves findings. Missing-evidence requests use fixed templates in the {EMAIL}, with approval before sending.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supporting documents varied, evidence was scattered and exceptions did not fit simple eligibility rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured validation is established technology. Bounded document extraction and cheaper integration development make the remaining preparation work more practical.
tasks.still_hard: Authenticity, conflicting evidence and legal interpretation remain difficult. A complete dossier does not establish eligibility by itself.
tasks.human_edge: Weigh contradictory evidence, interpret obligations and recognise when specialist legal advice is needed.

ambition.what: Permit-readiness preflight for proposed operational projects

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from searching documents to reviewing evidence and advising project owners before submission. The officer can recommend readiness; authority to grant permits or determine legal liability does not change.

reach.task: Validate financial evidence used in eligibility assessments.

evidence.claim: Veeva RIM tracks registrations and submissions, supporting the feasibility of controlled regulatory dossier management.
Source-linked extraction can reduce evidence preparation, but the digest supplies no measured eligibility-review outcome.
A determining score can engage GDPR automated-decision protections; advisory labels alone do not settle the issue.

assumptions: The company reviews its own obligations or counterparties rather than exercising public licensing powers.
Incomplete cases repeat evidence collection and assessment before final findings.
The document-heavy prior supports extraction, but low rule coverage keeps substantive assessment human.
GDPR and the EU AI Act require use-specific assessment; national consultation may apply.
Build ranges include access and applicable consultation in working days; statutory procedures can extend the calendar.
unknowns: Which eligibility criteria are explicit, versioned and approved?
Which documents contain personal or special-category data?
What authority does the officer have to finalise findings?
How often are documents unreadable, contradictory or suspected to be false?
Are supported interfaces available for financial records and case files?
research_questions: Which facts can be validated against authoritative records?
What evidence omissions could materially change an assessment?
Does the proposed processing require a DPIA or fall within an EU AI Act high-risk use?
new_work: Verify material extracted facts and source passages.
Maintain required fields and versioned assessment criteria.
Monitor extraction errors, permissions and retention.
Retest document handling when submission formats change.

tasks.short: Advise employees and counterparties on licence and permit requirements within the company's remit.

steps.what: Receive the question and identify the activity, jurisdiction and deadline.
Find current obligations and approved guidance for the stated activity and jurisdiction.
Clarify missing facts and the practical decision the requester needs to make.
Draft an explanation of requirements, next actions and unresolved issues.

loop.input: Clarified request and current approved guidance selected by jurisdiction and activity.
loop.output: Draft advice with source passages, next actions and explicit unresolved questions.
loop.check: Reject unsupported citations and expired guidance; the officer checks applicability and material claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per request; absent or conflicting guidance routes to specialist review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Case-specific explanations require combining facts with varied guidance; fixed answers cover only routine questions.

steps.what: Approve the interpretation or refer unresolved legal questions to legal counsel.
Explain the approved advice and answer questions about practical next steps.
Log advice, sources and agreed follow-up actions.

tasks.design: An intake form in the {WORKFLOW} selects current guidance in the {DOCS} by activity and jurisdiction. Fixed answers cover routine questions, while a bounded loop drafts explanations for more varied requests. The officer approves case-specific advice, handles the conversation and confirms the resulting advice record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Guidance lacked reliable jurisdiction and version tags. Questions often arrived without enough facts to choose an answer.
tasks.enabler_now: A controlled guidance index supports deterministic retrieval. Bounded drafting can turn selected guidance into clearer explanations without searching beyond approved sources.
tasks.still_hard: Applicability, regulatory change and implied reliance on advice remain difficult. Maintaining the guidance library takes continuing expert time.
tasks.human_edge: Discover the real business question, explain uncertainty and recognise when advice exceeds delegated expertise.

ambition.what: Permit guidance sessions for frontline purchasing coordinators

tasks.altitude: The officer spends less time searching and drafting, and more time on practical guidance and difficult interpretations. They can offer sessions to purchasing coordinators; legal interpretation rights remain subject to existing delegation.

reach.task: Assess the cash and timing impact of permit requirements.
reach.learn: Cash-flow dependencies, project commitments and funding approval.

evidence.claim: Controlled retrieval and bounded drafting are feasible patterns; the digest contains no direct licensing-advice deployment.
A documented report failure involved nonexistent sources, supporting explicit citation checks before advice is used.

assumptions: The typical corporate remit concerns business licences and permits; passport determinations belong to competent authorities.
Approved guidance has jurisdiction, effective-date and owner metadata.
Routine requests may skip clarification or a live explanation; the shares represent a mixed caseload.
The approval in s5 supplies the action gate in s6; unresolved legal questions require counsel clearance.
GDPR applies to request records; national consultation requirements depend on the implementation.
Build estimates include guidance setup, access and applicable consultation in working days.
unknowns: Which jurisdictions and licence categories are in scope?
Who approves guidance updates and difficult interpretations?
How frequently do requesters need live explanations?
Which requesters may access each guidance category?
Does an approved, current guidance library already exist?
research_questions: Which recurring questions can be answered safely with fixed approved text?
How will source changes invalidate earlier guidance and open advice drafts?
Which facts must be collected before advice can be applicable?
new_work: Maintain guidance versions, jurisdiction tags and access permissions.
Review draft applicability and supporting sources.
Route novel questions to legal counsel.
Confirm follow-up actions and correct advice records.
Turn recurring resolved questions into approved fixed answers.

tasks.short: Prepare compliance reports with verified evidence, evaluations, recommendations and decisions.

steps.what: Collect case records, approved findings, advice records and financial evidence.
Reconcile case totals, dates and financial amounts in a reporting workbook.
Evaluate significant findings and agree recommendations with control owners.
Write the report with evidence, metrics, conclusions and recommendations.

loop.input: Validated metrics, approved findings, human conclusions and a controlled report template.
loop.output: Report narrative linked to evidence; deterministic tables retain their validated values.
loop.check: Compare all figures with validated metrics, verify source references and check that conclusions match approved inputs.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per report; unsupported statements are removed or returned to the officer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables and fixed sections are deterministic, but a readable synthesis of varied findings needs bounded drafting.

steps.what: Approve conclusions, recommendations, disclosures and the intended audience.
Send the approved report to authorised recipients.
Archive the approved report, evidence references and distribution record.

tasks.design: Scheduled jobs on the {DATA_PLATFORM} collect controlled records from the {WORKFLOW}, {ERP} and {DOCS}, reconcile metrics and feed the {BI}. A report generator inserts validated tables and uses a bounded loop for narrative based on human conclusions. Approval in the {WORKFLOW} releases the exact report to its authorised audience through the {EMAIL} and archives its evidence in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports required repeated collection and workbook reconciliation. Recommendations depended on context that was poorly captured in source records.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic joins, reconciliations and templates are established. AI-assisted coding lowers assembly effort, while bounded drafting can work from approved conclusions.
tasks.still_hard: Data definitions, evidence completeness and materiality remain expensive to resolve. Narrative can overstate what the evidence establishes.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a technical exception from a material compliance failure and recommend a proportionate response.

ambition.what: Weekly prioritisation of remediation funding requests

tasks.altitude: The officer spends less time assembling periodic reports and can bring current evidence to weekly funding discussions. They gain a stronger recommendation role; budget approval remains with the financial manager.

reach.learn: Metric definitions, data lineage and reconciliation controls.
Cost-benefit assessment, financial exposure and budget constraints.

evidence.claim: Records, reconciliations, dashboards and report tables are suitable for deterministic automation; estimates are not measured outcomes.
Veeva RIM supports controlled regulatory submissions, an adjacent capability rather than proof of general compliance-report automation.
A documented government-report failure included nonexistent sources, supporting evidence checks before report release.

assumptions: The reporting workbook currently bridges case and financial records; some companies already perform these checks in the {BI}.
Report conclusions are supplied by people rather than inferred as binding decisions by the drafting loop.
The approval in s5 supplies the release gate in s6, including approval of any external recipients.
The report-writing prior supports drafting automation, but evaluation and recommendation work remain substantial.
GDPR governs personal data in reports; access, retention and national consultation requirements are assessed during setup.
Build ranges are working-day estimates and include applicable consultation; formal approval timelines may extend them.
unknowns: Which reports are internal, contractual or regulatory?
Are metrics defined consistently across source systems?
Which recipients and disclosures require additional approval?
What retention, evidence and submission requirements apply?
Do reports include employee-level monitoring or sensitive case details?
research_questions: Which report sections can be generated entirely from structured records?
How should corrected source records affect previously approved reports?
What reconciliation tolerances are appropriate for each financial measure?
new_work: Resolve reconciliation exceptions before report generation.
Review narrative against evidence and approved conclusions.
Maintain metric definitions, templates and recipient permissions.
Monitor failed extracts, delivery failures and archive completeness.
Retest connectors when source schemas change.

role.altitude: The compliance officer moves from document assembly and status chasing toward evidence assessment, practical advice and earlier remediation discussions. Legal, licensing, sanction and budget authority remain within existing delegations.
reach: Financial risk assessment of overdue remedies.
Financial planning for permit dependencies and remediation.
Reliable compliance metrics with the business intelligence analyst.
skills_to_grow: Translate approved obligations into testable checks.
Assess evidence provenance and contradictory records.
Define metrics and reconcile case data with financial records.
Assess GDPR, EU AI Act and applicable national consultation requirements.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a permit-readiness preflight service and bring current evidence to weekly remediation funding decisions, while retaining human assessment of disputed facts and legal consequences.
